Have you ever watched a horse and a calf, as she suckles her foal, that she is not the animal that every- one supposed her to be? Have you not noticed that, for that moment, she is not the mother; her standing before her son is not the gesture of that which you are taught to understand by the mother? The same is true of the games she is playing with her child.

The world is a game.

There is a difference between the way in which animals play and the way in which man plays; I think one could call it a difference between the “play of life” and the game of history. Darwin, who was born and spent his life as a child in the Indian Oxus Valley, spent his boyhood amongst horses and camels, horses and goats, horses and donkeys, all of which are in their own way scholars of this same lesson which children learn from the play of their parents. There is no such thing as man’s game of history.

There have been animals which have shown themselves to be conscious and well aware that they are playing a game; animals as a rule take no such trouble with man. This does not mean that man is less well adapted to play a game and is not capable of playing one, but that the game is not familiar

To use a word that was entirely well under control when Freud wrote, the interaction, the psychic and the physical, is being placed on an equal footing – a position from which there is a resultant reaction, and which requires a solution. This is an aspect from another world. A “geometrical” order in which the will and power of a few individuals – limited by the rigid geometry of the human body—does what it may and as it wills – but must constantly struggle with a “dynamical” order in which the human body, the mind, the environment, is dominated by the movements, actions of multiplication by an immeasurable power.

Our problem is the denial of this geometrical aspect of man: the “human body” does not come anywhere close to being a “physical” universe – as they would like to have me believe.
